thread:
morgan: FYI I ran a postmortem draft for the air-gapped delivery gap last week. one idea: keep a small replay buffer + manifest tombstone to allow replays when hub->operator jobs fail.
lina: replay buffer meaning we keep N recent manifests on the hub and allow operator to request a specific seq id?
raj: yes, but operator pulls are expensive for limited bandwidth sites. we should support a compact tombstone that summarizes deltas so operator can choose resume points without fetching full history.
alexa: sketch: hub keeps last 7 manifests plus a tombstone index that maps file -> chunk ranges + checksums + minimal apply-order metadata. operator asks: "give me earliest missing seq >= X" and hub responds with smallest delta patchlet.
morgan: exact. and add a mode where operator can request a "fast-verify snapshot": hub supplies a signed content-hash manifest and a short proof (per-chunk checksums). operator can stream only chunks that differ.
janet: we need to be explicit about signer rotation. if signer key changes mid-window, operator must still accept previously-signed manifests for replay until tombstone expiry. that implies tombstone must carry `signed_by` history.
lina: TTL concerns: on very low-bandwidth sites we might need longer retention than 7 manifests. make retention configurable per-customer and based on sync frequency. default 7 is just a suggestion.
raj: operator API additions proposal:
```http
POST /replay-request
{
  "want_seq": 1723,
  "capabilities": ["delta-patchlet","chunk-resume"],
  "max_bytes": 104857600
}
```
response: stream of patchlets + final tombstone-signed header.
alexa: also include a `replay_id` so retries are idempotent and we can revoke a replay if we detect suspicious behavior.
morgan: security note: replay buffers increase surface area for malicious injection if hub is compromised. recommend HSM-signed tombstone headers and an audit trail: `replay_id`, `issued_by`, `issued_at`, `retention_ms`.
janet: on the operator side we need an `apply_state` machine that can represent: `idle`, `receiving`, `verifying`, `pending_apply`, `applied`, `replay_failed`. admins should be able to inspect and force-advance `pending_apply` with strict rate limits.
lina: UX: Console should show per-site retention, last-replay-id, and bytes-saved-by-delta. gives SRE data to tune retention.
raj: testing: add an e2e harness scenario that simulates partial chunk loss and verifies `chunk-resume` works and final manifest verification passes. also measure end-to-end time vs full-image rebootstrap.
alexa: operationally we should combine with emergency-republish flow: if a critical CVE hotfix lands, hub can promote a replay buffer entry to `emergency` that short-circuits normal backoff but still uses token-limited streaming.
morgan: good catch. include `emergency` flag and `emergency_ttl_ms`. when set, hub will keep extra retention and operator token-bucket allows limited emergency streams.
janet: someone should own cleanup: periodic GC job that removes replay entries older than retention and emits a tombstone-eviction event to audit log.
ops-bot: note: retention change for customer-acme submitted as billing override request #5467 :information_source:
morgan: next steps: i'll open RFC issue with diagrams (hub buffer layout, operator apply-state FSM, signed tombstone format), and a short security appendix on signer rotation. lina/raj/alexa to review.
lina: i'll add the e2e spec snippets.
raj: i'll prototype the minimal API shard for replay-request.
alexa: i'll draft the tombstone header proto and signer rotation notes.
morgan: thanks. we should also add an alert: if per-site replay success rate drops below 95% for 1h, page oncall.
janet: agreed. and add a runbook step to temporarily increase retention for a site under remediation.
morgan: filing RFC now and will ping when it's up.
